subject: Weekly priority lane clearance and QBR readiness
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, Sarah Mills <sarah@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Weekly priority lane clearance and QBR readiness

Team —

Quick weekly update ahead of the QBR prep window. TL;DR: progress on two runway blockers, one escalation that needs a decision this week, and three asks (one for leadership).

Wins:
- Model onboarding: Dedicated runtime validation for the 7B quantized variant completed for ACE-47 workload (latency within target at 95th percentile).
- Cost ops: prototype batching policy reduced average per-token cost for non-interactive batch jobs by ~14% in the staging pool.
- CS: initial renewal conversation with Acme Health moved to procurement review (positive product fit signals).

Risks / Hotspots:
1) Dedicated pool autoscaler: we saw two incidents where the autoscaler did not pick up bursts for ~5m each (root cause: race in capacity reconciliation). If unresolved, this could impact QBR demos for enterprise customers next week.
2) Eval regressions: a small quality drop on instruction-following for X3 prompts when using the new kernel set; triggers failing quality gates in the Optimize pipeline.
3) Contract terms: Acme asked for an expanded data retention policy and an audit log export cadence that is slightly outside our standard offering. Procurement will want a clear escalation path.

Asks (action owners):
- Engineering (Karthik): please prioritize a short patch to autoscaler reconciliation and share an ETA by EOD Wednesday. If we can get a canary fix to prod, we avoid escalation in the demos. (owner: karthik_iyer)
- Product (Laura): sign off on fallback demo plan (we'll fall back to hosted region if dedicated pool throttles). Need a one-line approval to proceed. (owner: laura_bennett)
- Sales/CS (Marissa): coordinate with Acme procurement on the retention ask. Please attach the proposed wording and an internal risk note on acceptance thresholds. (owner: marissa_cole)

Attachments: I uploaded a compact priority-lane export and the QBR runbook draft for this week (see links + attachments listed below).

Next steps: Karthik + Eng to confirm autoscaler ETA; Laura to provide fallback approval; Marissa to update on procurement thread. If leadership has any objections to the fallback plan, call it out in-reply.

Thanks,
Olga

--
Olga Petrov
Head of Operations, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com
(Attachment: QBR-runbook-v2.pdf (overview), priority-lane.csv (workload export))

Subject: Re: Weekly priority lane clearance and QBR readiness

Folks —

Short update from engineering on the autoscaler and the eval regression:

Autoscaler (race condition): we reproduced the reconciliation gap in staging and have a targeted patch that forces atomic updates during snapshot reconciliation. I expect a canary in the staging "canary-3" pool by EOD Tuesday (2028-06-05) and a limited rollout to one prod shard by Friday if canary metrics look stable. I'll publish telemetry gating thresholds in the runbook.

Eval regression: the kernel selection change exposes a subtle numerical difference for a small set of instruct templates. We're rolling back the selection for production-critical models while we run a more exhaustive calibration on the nightly evals. That should be non-disruptive to customers; we'll monitor model-level metrics in the Optimize dashboard.

Attachments: QBR-runbook-v2.pdf (minor edits include telemetry gating and rollback steps), priority-lane.csv (filtered export).

ETA summary:
- Autoscaler canary to staging: 2028-06-05 17:00 PDT
- Limited prod rollout decision: 2028-06-07 (contingent on canary metrics)
- Eval rollback completed for affected models: 2028-06-02

I'll tag the runbook with the gating thresholds and link the canary dashboards.

Karthik
Lead, Serving Runtime
